summary: Malheur NF lookout in Grant County, OR: a 20-ft L-4 tower built 1933 on Sheep Mountain, staffed into 1953; now gone, with no removal date in sources.

facts.location: Malheur National Forest, Grant County, Oregon
facts.status_note: Tower gone; the Forest Lookouts page records its removal without a date, and no source describes the summit today

access.note: No source we read says whether the site is open to visitors

events.note: 20-foot native timber pole tower with an L-4 cab
Max O'Brien, the telephone operator, was stationed there; Mrs. O'Brien was in charge of the switchboard
Old tower described as 'stubbed' in 1947 (1953 entry)
New native wood tower placed under the existing house
Mr. and Mrs. Dick Martin and Mike stationed at the lookout
Registered July 16, 2011 as US 1090, OR 447; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com gives the pole as 15 ft; the register and the Forest Lookouts page give 20 ft. The 20-ft figure, which two sources agree on, is used.

notes_for_editor: Removal date is not given in any source read. The record's 20-ft (6.1 m) height is kept; firelookout.com gives 15 ft. The height_m value is the total pole height, not the cab floor. Several other pages on the web are named Sheep Mountain lookouts in Washington, Idaho, Montana and Wyoming; they were not used, and the Washington Republic News-Miner quotes on washingtonlookouts.weebly.com must not be attributed to this site. The NGS survey text is quoted on the Forest Lookouts page and was not checked against NGS directly. No photos added.
